scope: Theorem 1.3 (Constant-additive hardness) of the manuscript “Additive hardness and unbounded configuration gaps in bin packing” (preprints/Additive-hardness-and-unbounded-configuration-gaps-in-bin-packing-September-24-2026/Additive-hardness-and-unbounded-configuration-gaps-in-bin-packing-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 118 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 cf1e9b383ad38a1c), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every fixed integer c ≥ 0, it is NP-hard to distinguish pairs (I, B) such that I packs into B bins from pairs such that I cannot be packed into B + c bins. Here B is an integer supplied with the instance, the item sizes are rational, and every item size is strictly greater than 1/6.
